title: Comparable-Housing Share of Loss of Use — Excess Flood Claims
content:
Loss of use paid on an **Excess Flood Policies (Surplus Lines)** claim is measured against comparable housing: a high monthly figure relative to the home's value is paid at a share.

## Rule

The comparable-housing share of the loss of use counted is 80 percent where the loss of use counted per displacement month exceeds 0.40 percent of the replacement cost value on the policy record, 90 percent where it exceeds 0.25 percent but not 0.40 percent, and the whole figure otherwise.

The loss of use counted is the figure incurred to date on the latest adjuster report of the claim. The displacement months are the whole months from the date of loss to the date of the latest adjuster report, counted as at least one. The claim is the claim of the policy that carries the latest adjuster report, and every claim figure is read from that claim's own entries.

Every share or period cut multiplies the loss of use counted; every amount deducted is then subtracted, never taking the figure below nothing; every allowance is then added; the loss-of-use limit then caps the result; payments already issued on the claim are subtracted after the cap; and every interest charge is added last.

| Loss of use counted per displacement month, as a percent of the replacement cost value | Share of the loss of use counted |
|---|---|
| above 0.40 | 80 percent (0.8) |
| above 0.25, up to and including 0.40 | 90 percent (0.9) |
| 0.25 or below | the whole figure |

## Boundaries (hypothetical, replacement cost value 1000000)

0.40 percent of 1000000 is 4000 a month and 0.25 percent is 2500. Loss of use of 24000 over 6 displacement months is 4000 a month — not above 0.40 percent — so 90 percent applies; 24001 over 6 months is above it and takes 80 percent. 15000 over 6 months is 2500 a month and the whole figure stands.
